title: EA-inequivalent bent four-concatenations outside the completed Maiorana--McFarland class
summary: Construct theoretically proved EA-inequivalent pairs of the source's four-concatenation form outside the completed Maiorana--McFarland class.

formal_statement.body: For even $n\ge 6$, let $g\in\mathcal B_n$ be bent and let $A,A'$ be affine permutations of $\mathbb F_2^n$. Set $h=g\circ A$, $h'=g\circ A'$, $f=g\|h\|g\|(h+1)$, and $f'=g\|h'\|g\|(h'+1)$ in $\mathcal B_{n+2}$. Construct a theoretically specified pair for which $f$ and $f'$ are bent, both lie outside $\mathcal M^{\#}$, and $f$ and $f'$ are EA-inequivalent; alternatively prove nonexistence under this form.

scope.domain: Bent four-concatenations, EA-equivalence, and the completed Maiorana--McFarland class
assumptions: $g$ is bent and $A,A'$ are affine permutations of $\mathbb F_2^n$
$f=g||h||g||(h+1)$ and $f'=g||h'||g||(h'+1)$ use the source concatenation convention
$\mathcal M^{\#}$ is the completed Maiorana--McFarland class and EA-equivalence is the source relation
scope.unresolved_remainder: Later Theorem 4.9 and Theorem 5.1-type results prove bentness and exclusion from $\mathcal M^{\#}$ for individual exact-form outputs, and report computationally inequivalent examples, but no inspected result proves a theoretically parameterized pair with a common $g$ and two affine permutations $A,A'$ together with the required EA-inequivalence argument.

progress.summary: Article 044 asks for theoretical EA-inequivalent pairs of the two exact four-concatenation forms outside the completed Maiorana--McFarland class.

Almost Maiorana--McFarland bent functions proves a broad one-output construction of the exact four-concatenation shape and exclusion from the completed class, but does not prove the requested two-output EA-inequivalence theorem.

The later permutation construction gives additional one-output bent four-concatenations outside the completed class, including an explicit finite instance, without proving the requested pairwise EA-inequivalence.
A later survey records the membership criterion and outside-class counting inequalities but does not establish the exact affine-permutation pair required by Open Problem 2.
